title: Redwood Security Review - SSO/SCIM/RBAC - EnterpriseCloud
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked EnterpriseCloud security and infra through SSO (SAML) setup, SCIM provisioning and group mapping, and recommended RBAC roles and least-privilege patterns. Key compliance topics (SOC 2, ISO) and encryption/KMS and audit log retention were discussed. Next steps include sharing SAML metadata, RBAC role matrix, SOC 2 report, scheduling an implementation call and pilot for SCIM provisioning.

Owner: Samir Patel | Item: Provide SCIM group-mapping template and sample payloads, include Delta provisioning notes | Due: 2026-12-10
Owner: Alex Carter | Item: Send RBAC role matrix recommended by Redwood with least-privilege defaults and mapping to EnterpriseCloud AD groups | Due: 2026-12-09
Owner: Priya Menon | Item: Provide list of required attributes (email, uid, department) and sample Okta config to Redwood | Due: 2026-12-07
Owner: Alex Carter | Item: Share SOC 2 Type II summary and ISO/attestation links; provide contact for compliance packet | Due: 2026-12-06
next_steps: Redwood to email SAML/SCIM/RBAC docs + SOC2 report
Schedule 60-min implementation call for SSO + SCIM on 2026-12-15

transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-12-04 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Rachel Kim (Head of Security, EnterpriseCloud), Tom Liu (SRE), Priya Menon (IAM Engineer), Michael Ortiz (Director, Compliance)

[00:00] Alex Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. um we'll kick off in a sec. i'm Alex, AE at Redwood, and Samir our solutions engineer is with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Rachel Kim: Good, thanks. busy quarter but excited to go through SSO and scim.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Awesome, quick agenda. We'll walk through SAML single sign-on setup, SCIM provisioning flow, recommended RBAC roles and least privilege mapping, and then cover audit logs, encryption / KMS and compliance artifacts. lots to get to so we'll be brief and then dive deep where you want.
[00:28] Tom Liu: Sounds good. we mostly want to confirm network constraints and how SAML interacts with our existing Okta flows.
[00:33] Priya Menon: Also want to make sure group sync won't create excess privileges; we need fine-grained mapping.
[00:38] Alex Carter: totally. we'll show the pattern we recommend: IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML both supported, metadata exchange, and a recommended attribute map. Samir, do you want to share the typical config?
[00:47] Samir Patel: Yeah. At a high level, Redwood expects the SAML assertion to include email (NameID) and an attribute for groups. Common setup is to map Okta "groups" to Redwood roles via SCIM or via the SAML groups claim if you prefer not to enable SCIM. But recommended path for enterprise is SCIM provisioning for automated user lifecycle + group mapping.
[01:10] Rachel Kim: So SCIM is required for group updates? we currently do SCIM for other vendors but need to understand delta vs full sync.
[01:18] Samir Patel: We support both. we recommend delta patch provisioning (the PATCH delta approach in RFC 7644) for efficiency. Full sync can be used as a fallback. Note that with delta provisioning you get near real-time group membership updates which is better for least-privilege enforcement.
[01:35] Michael Ortiz: From compliance perspective we also need audit trail of role changes - who changed what and when. How does Redwood store that? retention windows?
[01:44] Samir Patel: Good Q. Redwood writes audit logs for auth events, role assignments, and provisioning activity to the customer audit log stream. For hosted customers we provide configurable retention - default 90 days, options to extend to 1 year or more under enterprise plan. We can also integrate with your SIEM via syslog or push to S3/GCS.
[02:05] Tom Liu: If we push logs to our S3, are they encrypted with our KMS?
[02:10] Alex Carter: Yes, for dedicated/private we can use customer-managed keys (CMKs) - HSM-backed KMS or cloud KMS. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS in enterprise setups.
[02:21] Priya Menon: A little clarifying question on RBAC. What are the out-of-the-box roles and can we create custom roles? we want least-privilege mapping from AD groups.
[02:30] Samir Patel: Redwood ships a default role set: Admin, Developer, Viewer, Billing. You can create custom roles with fine-grained permissions - down to endpoints/actions like generate, manage-models, view-audit-logs. Best practice: two admin seats only, dev roles scoped to deploy/route but not bill, etc. We'll provide a role matrix sample.
[02:50] Rachel Kim: Do you support attribute-based access control (ABAC) or only RBAC?
[02:55] Samir Patel: Right now main control plane is RBAC, but you can implement ABAC-style patterns using SCIM group attributes + custom roles. We're tracking ABAC requirements for roadmap but not GA yet.
[03:06] Michael Ortiz: About SAML specifics - entity IDs, ACS URLs, cert rotation. we need to know cert rotation cadence and how to handle rollover without downtime.
[03:16] Alex Carter: We support key rollover with multiple cert slots in metadata so you can publish a new cert before switching. We'll share our SP metadata with two certs to help with rollover.
[03:26] Tom Liu: Ok good. on network, we are planning a private deployment in a VPC; does the SAML redirect flow require public endpoints?
[03:34] Samir Patel: If you're doing purely private with no public access, you can do SAML over your internal SSO if you host the Redwood control plane in your VPC (private deployment). For hosted Redwood there are public endpoints and you can restrict access via IP allowlists and SAML assertions. We'll document both patterns.
[03:54] Rachel Kim: One of our blockers historically is account provisioning freshness. If SCIM lags does that mean someone might retain old privileges?
[04:01] Samir Patel: It depends on the cadence. With delta SCIM patches, changes apply within seconds to minutes. With full sync daily, there is a window. We recommend event-driven delta for security-sensitive groups.
[04:14] Priya Menon: Can SCIM map nested groups? our AD uses nested groups a lot.
[04:19] Samir Patel: We support flat group mapping out of the box. For nested groups you'd either flatten in the IdP (Okta has a flattening rule) or we can work with you on a custom mapping during pilot.
[04:34] Michael Ortiz: For audit logs, are the logs tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody assurances for SOC 2.
[04:41] Samir Patel: For enterprise, logs can be exported to your storage where you control integrity. For hosted logs, we provide integrity markers and write-once options for the audit stream; our SOC 2 report describes controls around log integrity and retention. We'll attach the SOC2 Type II summary.
[04:58] Alex Carter: I'll note that and share the compliance packet.
[05:02] Rachel Kim: Encryption at rest and in transit - are keys customer-managed in hosted? you said envelope but wanted detail.
[05:09] Alex Carter: Right - hosted uses envelope encryption with service-managed keys by default. Under enterprise we can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integrated with AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault/GCP KMS and HSM-backed keys for private stacks. Transit TLS 1.2+ enforced and we support mTLS for dedicated/private setups.
[05:25] Tom Liu: Good. Any SOC2 scoping gaps you often see with folks integrating SSO?
[05:31] Samir Patel: The common annex is around provisioning lifecycle and orphaned accounts. Make sure SCIM deprovisions users promptly and that service accounts are audited. Also ensure MFA enforcement; Redwood respects IdP MFA and you can require certain auth context.
[05:47] Priya Menon: How do we handle service accounts vs human users? we want different RBAC for machine tokens.
[05:53] Samir Patel: You can create API keys scoped to service roles with restricted scopes and expiry. For high-sensitivity ops we recommend short-lived keys and rotating credentials via our API. We'll share best practices.
[06:10] Alex Carter: i'll pause and ask, Rachel - what are your must-haves to get to an internal signoff?
[06:16] Rachel Kim: We need SAML integration docs, proof of SCIM delta provisioning, role matrix with least-privilege mapping, SOC2 Type II, and confirmation of KMS BYOK. Also a proposed retention for audit logs that meets our policy - 365 days ideally.
[06:28] Alex Carter: perfect. We'll provide that packet. Next - technical deep-dive - Samir, could you run through an example SAML attribute mapping and a SCIM delta sample?
[06:38] Samir Patel: Sure. Example SAML assertion: NameID = user@example.com, attributes: groups = ["infra-admins","data-science"], email_verified = true. On SCIM side PATCH /Users/{id} with operations add/remove for group membership. Here's a sample delta payload... (Samir reads a small JSON sample - transcription note: speaker reads code)
[07:05] Tom Liu: ok makes sense. you mentioned the groups claim - can we limit which groups get sent to Redwood?
[07:10] Samir Patel: yes use claim filters in Okta or AAD to only include mapped groups. Also use SCIM to control exact group membership.
[07:17] Priya Menon: For attribute requirements - do we need the internal employee id or email is enough?
[07:22] Samir Patel: Email as NameID is sufficient for mapping, but internal uid helps avoid email-based duplicates. We'll list required and optional attributes in the doc.
[07:31] Rachel Kim: On provisioning sequencing, if we provision a user with SCIM but they haven't accepted SSO yet, are they blocked?
[07:38] Samir Patel: You can provision accounts in an inactive state until SAML assertion first-time login, or auto-activate. It's configurable.
[07:46] Michael Ortiz: A compliance question: do you maintain change logs for RBAC role edits and who edited them?
[07:52] Samir Patel: Yes role edits are recorded with timestamp and actor; that's in the audit stream. For hosted customers we surface change history in the console and allow export.
[08:02] Tom Liu: For the pilot, we'd like to test group mapping, certificate rollover, and log export. what's a reasonable timeline?
[08:09] Alex Carter: Typically a 2-week pilot for SCIM + SAML is feasible; 1 week for setup and config, 1 week for validation. We'll need access to a test Okta tenant and sample users.
[08:20] Rachel Kim: We'll try to schedule the implementation call mid-december, like you suggested.
[08:24] Priya Menon: can you also include the sample syslog/S3 export configurations so we can pre-provision buckets with correct IAM?
[08:31] Samir Patel: yes we'll include S3 bucket policy, KMS key policy examples and how to configure endpoint signing.
[08:38] Alex Carter: quick note: we sometimes see customers ask about multi-tenant implications of SCIM - if you have multiple orgs within your account you can map separate SCIM connectors or use group prefixes. we can go into that in the pilot.
[08:52] Rachel Kim: Regarding data residency - our regulation requires EU data residency for certain tenants. can Redwood pin logs and inference data to EU regions?
[08:59] Samir Patel: We can route traffic and store data in EU-only regions for dedicated/private customers. For hosted multi-region we have regional storage options; for strict residency we recommend dedicated capacity in the target region or private deployment.
[09:14] Michael Ortiz: on encryption and keys, if we bring our own key, who's responsible for key rotation?
[09:20] Alex Carter: Customers own key lifecycle for BYOK. We support rotation via key aliases and multiple key versions. We'll provide the KMS integration guide.
[09:28] Tom Liu: Any rate limits on SCIM PATCH operations? we have automated group updates that can be chatty.
[09:34] Samir Patel: For enterprise we lift default rate limits or provide a dedicated endpoint with higher throughput. We'll size based on your expected provisioning volume.
[09:41] Priya Menon: One more - can we attach org-level approval workflow when someone requests elevated roles?
[09:47] Samir Patel: Not natively, but you can tie role elevation requests to your internal approval workflow and then trigger SCIM group changes which map to Redwood roles. We're prebuilt with webhooks to hook into approval systems.
[09:59] Alex Carter: ok, wrapping toward the end - any outstanding blockers?
[10:03] Rachel Kim: Documentation and the SOC 2 are key; also need clarity on log retention and BYOK details - those are our acceptance criteria.
[10:11] Alex Carter: noted. We'll send the packet and set up the implementation. Samir, any final technical notes?
[10:16] Samir Patel: Just that for nested groups we'll propose a flattening rule and include a script example. Also mention we'll provide a temporary demo tenant for testing SCIM.
[10:28] Michael Ortiz: Good. A couple people might want to have follow-up with security - can we get a 30-minute compliance-only session?
[10:33] Alex Carter: Absolutely, we'll coordinate.
[10:36] Rachel Kim: great. thanks everyone.
[10:38] Alex Carter: Thanks all - recap and next steps in chat.

Recap (auto): Redwood to share SAML metadata, SCIM docs and delta patch samples, RBAC role matrix, SOC2 docs, KMS integration guide, and S3/syslog export examples. Schedule implementation call 2026-12-15. Customer to prepare Okta test tenant and AD group mappings.
